Question Text: Sort these urban features by how much they actually affect your happiness.
Objective: Measure stated desire vs actual lifestyle impact.
Exact Options: Items: Green spaces, Late-night food, Fast transit, Quiet streets, Local coffee shops | Buckets: Dealbreaker, Nice to have, Rarely use
Expected Result Shape: Green spaces highly retained across demographics.
Why This Question Exists: Moves beyond standard urbanism surveys into actual utility.
What Makes It Interesting: Reveals the gap between aspirational city living and reality.
Alternative Versions: What do you want in a city?

Question Text: Swipe: Is this public behavior acceptable or a crime against society?

Personal Insight Type: You are more forgiving than X% of users.
Expected Result Shape: Cart returning and escalator stopping will be universally hated.
Why This Question Exists: High-reach chaos engine disguised as urbanism.

Question Text: You can only save one for your neighborhood. Choose.
Exact Options: Thriving independent local businesses | Cheap and abundant parking
Why This Question Exists: Tests the core tension in modern urban planning.
What Makes It Interesting: People usually want both; forcing a choice reveals true priorities.
Rejected Alternatives: Would you give up your car?
Notes: Excellent for secondary Geographic map visualization.

Question Text: Rank these transit friction points from 'Minor annoyance' to 'Day ruined'.

Expected Result Shape: Missing train takes top tier for urbanites, traffic for suburbanites.
What Makes It Interesting: Turns a boring commute survey into an emotional release.
